title: Choose the look for Eunomia
question: Every option is San Francisco startup grade. The roll picked Multiplayer Canvas. Keep it, take Linear-grade Workspace, or re-roll.

options.label: Multiplayer Canvas
options.lineage: Figma, tldraw and Excalidraw: the shared canvas SF teams live in
options.thesis: Your agents are teammates in the room: every memory carries a named, coloured cursor tag for the agent that wrote it.
options.viewport: Dashboard opens on a dot-grid canvas header: live presence row of connected agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) as coloured cursor chips, then a dense memory activity table where every row shows its author chip and age.
options.risk: If the cursor chips get cute it reads as a toy; they must stay small, factual and tied to real provenance.

raised.raise: Live rows update in place inside fixed tabular columns: values change, layout never moves.
The blue accent is reserved for things you can press or have selected; agent colours only mark authorship.
Every hairline and border renders at exactly one device pixel; no soft 2px borders anywhere.
Entity and connector detail is prefetched on hover so the next view is already loaded one click away.

options.label: Linear-grade Workspace
options.lineage: Linear, Vercel, Raycast: keyboard-first SF dev tools
options.thesis: A fast, keyboard-first workspace: near-monochrome, one violet accent, Cmd-K as the front door.
options.viewport: Slim sidebar, a big Cmd-K hint, stat strip, then a dense list of sources and recent memories with keyboard shortcuts on every row.
options.risk: This is where most SF dev tools land: it looks right but could be mistaken for any Linear clone.

options.label: Split-flap concourse board
options.thesis: Memory activity as a departure board with flipping characters.
options.viewport: A board of live recalls and writes cascading per character.
options.case: Fuses as a live activity board but reads as a transit gimmick to engineering teams.
options.kept: Fixed columns that never move; only values change.

options.label: Warm consumer app surface
options.thesis: Soft cards, warm ground, one action colour.
options.viewport: Single column of big friendly cards with a bottom bar.
options.case: Too soft and sparse for teams scanning dense memory data.
options.kept: One colour reserved strictly for actions.
options.risk: Feels like a consumer app, not team infrastructure.

options.label: Centre-rail reference setting
options.thesis: Two text columns around a rail of keys.
options.case: Beautiful for docs, wrong world for an operating console.

options.label: Vertical feed surface
options.thesis: One memory per screen, snap to the next.
options.case: Kills density; teams need to scan many rows.
options.kept: The next item is already loaded one step away.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean shadcn-style SaaS dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, KPI cards, a chart and a table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other SaaS dashboard by design.
